strings.name: Ramon Laguarta
strings.role: PepsiCo Chairman and CEO; IBM Director
strings.summary: Ramon Laguarta is a Spanish executive who joined PepsiCo in 1996. After European and group leadership roles, he became CEO in 2018 and chairman in 2019. He advanced international business, portfolio and supply-chain changes; his tenure saw the launch of pep+ and the acquisition of poppi. Subsequent sustainability-target revisions and commercial results require separate assessment.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. Distinguish president, CEO, chairman and outside director roles, as well as transaction completion, brand promotion and actual outcomes. Birth is supported only to the year given by secondary sources; environmental targets are not completed achievements.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads PepsiCo’s global food and beverage business, participating in product, supply-chain and brand strategy changes.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: MBA from ESADE Business School in Spain and a Master in International Management from Thunderbird School of Global Management.
strings.facts.f2.label: Role transitions
strings.facts.f2.value: Became PepsiCo CEO on 3 October 2018 and chairman on 1 February 2019; joined IBM’s board on 1 March 2026.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Reshaping the food and beverage portfolio
strings.highlights.h1.text: Expanded business through brand, channel and supply-chain strategies, completing the poppi acquisition in 2025; acquisition does not establish a product’s health benefits.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Sustainability strategy and revised targets
strings.highlights.h2.text: Launched pep+ in 2021; in 2025 the company changed its net-zero goal from 2040 to 2050 or sooner and revised packaging targets.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Comments on quarterly operations
strings.timeline.t1.text: The earnings release quoted his comments on international operations and North American improvement plans; proposed cost actions were not yet achieved results.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Joining IBM’s board
strings.timeline.t2.text: Became an IBM director while continuing to lead PepsiCo, without becoming IBM’s operating chief.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Completion of poppi acquisition
strings.timeline.t3.text: PepsiCo completed its acquisition of the soda brand poppi; closing is distinct from the earlier agreement.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Launch of pep+ strategy
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company introduced a transformation framework covering agriculture, value chains and product choices, including environmental targets later revised.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Adding the PepsiCo chairmanship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Indra Nooyi as chairman, after the start of his CEO tenure.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becoming PepsiCo CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Succeeded Indra Nooyi and joined the board; the August announcement is not treated as the effective start date.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becoming group president
strings.timeline.t7.text: Moved from leadership of Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa to group president, with responsibilities including corporate strategy.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joining PepsiCo
strings.timeline.t8.text: Moved from Chupa Chups to PepsiCo, initially as marketing vice president for the Spanish snacks business.
